metaDescription: Blueair Blue Pure 211i, 311i, 511i, DustMagnet, Signature and Mini Max compared by room size, noise and filter design to help you choose the right one.
expertTake: The Blue Pure 311i Max is the sensible all-rounder for most bedrooms and living rooms, while the 211i Max is the one for open plans. The Blue 511 is the budget entry to the brand's quiet design. Anyone who wants carbon-heavy odor removal should look at the Signature line or a different brand entirely.
introParagraphs: Quiet operation is the reason people choose one purifier family over another, and this brand has built its identity around it. The design idea is to make filtration easy on the fan so it can move plenty of air without a loud motor.

That philosophy shows up in bedrooms first, where noise decides whether a machine stays on overnight. It also comes with trade-offs in odor handling and filter pricing that are worth understanding before you buy.

products.name: Blueair Blue Pure 311i Max WiFi purifier
products.description:
The 311i Max is where the brand's quiet-first approach pays off for the widest range of homes. HEPASilent combines electrostatic charging with a mechanical pleated layer, which means the filter does not need to be packed tight to catch fine particles, and the fan can turn slowly while still moving a useful volume of air.

The tradeoff is that the carbon content is modest, so cooking and pet odors are handled less decisively than in carbon-heavy machines. It also uses an auto mode driven by a sensor rather than a fixed speed, which lets the fan idle most of the day. Against the 511i Max it covers a much larger listed area, while against the 211i Max it is simply a smaller machine, not a different design.

Ownership is about swapping one combined filter on the schedule the app reminds you of, plus occasionally vacuuming the cloth pre-filter sleeve. The washable fabric exterior can be changed for a different color if the look matters in a living room.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and medium living rooms where quiet running matters most.
pros: HEPASilent design allows low fan noise
Auto mode idles quietly between spikes
Washable cloth pre-filter sleeve
App scheduling and filter reminders
cons: Replacement filter is a recurring cost

products.name: Blueair Blue Pure 211i Max large-room purifier
products.description:
For open plans and large lounges, the 211i Max is the machine in this family built to keep up. It uses the same HEPASilent approach as its smaller siblings but with a larger filter and a bigger fan, so the listed coverage of 3,235 square feet is the highest here.

The larger body makes it a presence in a room, and it asks for clear space on the intake side. At low speeds it stays whisper-quiet, but pushed to maximum for smoke events it becomes clearly audible, as any machine moving this much air does. It is a smarter choice than running two smaller units only if the space is genuinely open.

Upkeep follows the family pattern: one combined filter and a washable pre-filter fabric. Because the filter is larger, replacement is pricier than for the 311i Max, so check the genuine part price before committing.
products.bestFor: Open-plan living areas and large rooms.
pros: Highest listed coverage in the lineup
Same quiet HEPASilent design in a large body
App and auto mode work as in the smaller units
Washable pre-filter fabric

products.name: Blueair Blue Pure 511i Max bedroom purifier
products.description:
The 511i Max is the right-sized machine for a bedroom or home office. A smaller footprint than the 311i Max, it keeps the same filtration type while dropping the listed coverage to 1,138 square feet, which matches a typical sleeping room with a modest margin.

Because the volume is small, the fan rarely has to climb above its low settings, and that is where the quiet reputation is earned. In a living room it would run near maximum all evening, which defeats the point. It makes sense to pair it with the 311i Max in a home that has both a family room and a nursery.

Upkeep is the same filter and fabric routine. The app reminders are useful here because a bedroom unit runs more hours than most owners realise.
products.bestFor: Sleeping rooms and offices up to a normal bedroom size.
pros: Compact tower fits a nightstand zone
Same HEPASilent filtration as larger models
Stays quiet because the room is small
App control and scheduling
cons: Same modest carbon load for odors

products.name: Blueair Blue Pure 511 compact purifier
products.description:
This is the stripped-down entry to the brand's quiet design: same dual filtration, a smaller listed area of 907 square feet and no WiFi. For a dorm room or small bedroom that does not need an app, it removes cost without removing what matters.

The control scheme is simple buttons rather than a sensor-driven auto mode, so you choose a speed. That suits people who dislike a purifier that changes its own sound, but it means you will forget it on high some nights. Next to the 511i Max it gives up smart features and about a quarter of the coverage.

The filter and fabric pre-filter are the only upkeep. Keep the sleeve vacuumed and the combined filter on schedule, and the compact body will run for years without drama.
products.bestFor: Small rooms where an app is unnecessary and quiet matters.
pros: Brand's quiet filtration in a compact body
No account or app required
Washable fabric pre-filter
Lower entry price within the brand
cons: Smaller listed coverage than the i-series
Manual speed only, no auto mode

products.name: Blueair DustMagnet 5440i dual-intake purifier
products.description:
The DustMagnet changes where the air is drawn from. A second intake near the floor targets dust before it settles, and a vortex airflow pattern keeps airborne dust moving toward the filter. That makes it a better fit for homes with pets, hardwood floors or people who see dust return within days of cleaning.

It does not replace sweeping, and it will not pick up hair stuck to the carpet. The extra floor-level intake also means you must keep that side clear of rugs and furniture, otherwise the design advantage disappears. In sound it is similar to the other quiet models, but its listed 1,608 square foot coverage sits between the 311i Max and 211i Max.

Upkeep centres on keeping the floor intake free of lint. Pet owners should vacuum the intake area monthly, in addition to the normal filter replacement.
products.bestFor: Homes with pets and hard floors where dust keeps coming back.
pros: Floor-level intake targets settling dust
Vortex airflow keeps dust in circulation
Quiet HEPASilent filtration
App enabled
cons: Needs clear space at the floor intake
Does not remove hair stuck in carpet

products.name: Blueair Signature SP4i seven-stage purifier
products.description:
The Signature line adds an odor stage to the brand's particle approach. A seven-stage filter with an OdorFence layer is aimed at cooking smell, pets and smoke residue, which the standard Blue Pure cartridges handle only modestly.

That extra filter media means a larger, more expensive replacement than the Blue Pure line, and it carries a premium purchase price as well. It also keeps the quiet running character, so you pay mostly for gas handling. If odors are not an issue, the 311i Max does nearly everything else for less.

Ownership is again a single replaceable filter on the app's schedule. Take it seriously: carbon-type layers saturate, so a late change shows up as returning smells before the fan shows any sign of trouble.
products.bestFor: Kitchens and open areas with cooking smells and pet odors.
pros: OdorFence stage targets cooking and pet odors
Seven-stage filtration beyond the Blue Pure
Same quiet-running philosophy
WiFi and auto detection
cons: Overkill if only dust is the issue

buyingCriteria.explanation: The brand's filter combines electrostatic charge with a pleated mechanical layer, so fine particles stick without needing a dense media that stresses the fan. The result is lower airflow resistance and a quieter motor. For you, that means the 311i Max can run at 23 dB listed on its low setting while still moving useful air. The catch is that the electrostatic effect does nothing for gases, so smell control needs a carbon layer.

A 3,235 square foot listing on the 211i Max assumes a lower air-change rate than allergy-grade cleaning needs. In a 300 square foot bedroom the same machine delivers many more changes per hour, which is why the 511i Max, listed at 1,138 square feet, is usually the correct bedroom pick. Over-buying coverage gives you quieter running, not worse cleaning.

Standard Blue Pure filters lean on the particle stage. The Signature SP4i adds an OdorFence layer, and that is the only model here designed for strong cooking smells and smoke residue. Choose it only when smell is a daily complaint, since it comes with a larger filter bill.

The i-series models read a particle sensor and adjust the fan, so the 311i Max idles quietly most of the time and ramps up when you cook. The Blue 511 has manual speeds only, which suits owners who dislike changing sound. Sensors can drift and read particles only, so do not expect them to detect gases.

One combined filter with a replacement interval of around six months is typical for the brand's line, and that is a recurring cost that compounds over five years. The Blue 511 and 511i Max use smaller filters than the 211i Max, which lowers each purchase. Always price the genuine replacement for your exact model before you buy.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Plan for floor and wall space
buyingCriteria.explanation: The DustMagnet 5440i needs its floor intake clear, the 211i Max needs open space on all sides to feed its larger fan, and the compact 511 models tolerate a nightstand. Placing a purifier in a corner or behind a couch quietly cuts effective airflow. A clear 12 inches around the intake is a sensible minimum.

specDecoder.meaning: A manufacturer estimate of the largest room the unit can serve at a stated air-change rate, not a guarantee. Smaller rooms get more air changes per hour than the figure suggests.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 211i Max at 3,235 square feet and the 511 at 907 square feet should be read as ceilings, not recommendations.

specDecoder.meaning: A combination of electrostatic and mechanical capture. It captures fine particles with less fan effort than a dense mechanical-only filter.
specDecoder.watchFor: Quietness comes from the design, but it does not add gas capture, which only the Signature SP4i's extra stage addresses.

specDecoder.meaning: Quoted at the lowest speed in a lab setting, and a decibel scale is logarithmic so small numbers hide large differences. The highest speed is much louder.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 23 dB of the 311i Max and 211i Max and 24 dB of the Blue 511 apply to the quietest setting only.

specDecoder.meaning: The marketing count of media layers, including pre-filter, particle and odor stages. More stages usually means more carbon and a pricier filter.
specDecoder.watchFor: On the Signature SP4i the added value is the OdorFence layer, not a tighter particle filter.

specDecoder.meaning: The unit connects to an app that logs air readings and schedules running. Auto mode changes fan speed from the sensor reading.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Blue 511 omits both, so choose it only if you want manual control.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise design
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each model's listed low-speed sound level and the filter design behind it. The 311i Max and 211i Max at 23 dB led the comparison. We discounted claims that only apply at the quietest setting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coverage fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Listed coverage was reduced to a realistic allergy-grade figure for each unit. Pairing room size to model, such as the 511i Max at 1,138 square feet for a bedroom, gave a fit score. Machines that only work when stretched were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration scope
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared particle design with gas handling, flagging which models carry an odor layer. The Signature SP4i stood alone with its OdorFence stage. The rest were rated for particle work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership cost
howWeEvaluated.description: Filter size and replacement frequency were compared across the family. Larger filters on the 211i Max and SP4i cost more per swap than the compact models. Price tier in the data fed the value ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Smart features
howWeEvaluated.description: App, auto mode and scheduling were checked against how they affect daily use. Owner feedback patterns suggest the sensor and reminders matter most in bedrooms. The Blue 511 was scored on manual simplicity instead.

cards.label: Blue Pure line
cards.text: Focus on particles and quiet running. The 311i Max, 211i Max and 511i Max all use HEPASilent, and replacement filters are cheaper than the Signature's.

cards.label: Signature line
cards.text: Adds an odor stage and a seven-stage filter in the SP4i. It costs more upfront and per filter, so it earns its place only where smells are a daily issue.

howToChoose.note: Pick Blue Pure for dust, pollen and pets; pick the SP4i for cooking and smoke odors.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Capture that reaches floor-level dust and a washable pre-filter that handles hair before it reaches the main filter. A larger intake area helps because hair loads the pre-stage quickly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DustMagnet 5440i pulls from a floor-level intake and is the best fit, while the 311i Max with its washable fabric sleeve is the better all-rounder if the dust is mostly airborne.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Cooking smell or smoke residue is the complaint, which makes the Signature SP4i worth its filter cost, or if the room is open and the 211i Max can replace two small units.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need pollen and dust control in a small room, where the Blue 511 or 511i Max does the same particle job.

maintenance.why: Hair and lint load the sleeve first. A clean sleeve protects the main filter and keeps airflow up.
The electrostatic effect weakens and the carbon layer saturates. Late swaps show up as returning smells and louder running.

maintenance.task: Wipe the housing and sensor window
maintenance.why: Dust on the sensor window skews auto readings. A dry microfiber cloth is enough.
Furniture and curtains creep toward the intake. The DustMagnet 5440i also needs its floor intake kept free of lint.
Follow the care label so the fabric stays dense. A damp sleeve must dry fully before refitting.

faq.q: Which Blueair is best for a bedroom?
faq.a: The 511i Max is sized for a normal bedroom and stays on low speeds, which is where it is quietest. The Blue 511 is the budget version without app features.

faq.q: Is a bigger model always better?
faq.a: No. A large unit in a small room can run at a lower speed and give more air changes with less noise, but it costs more and occupies more floor. Match the model to the room first and spend more only if you want the quieter margin.
The standard Blue Pure models handle particles well but carry a modest odor layer. The Signature SP4i adds an OdorFence stage designed for cooking smell and smoke.

faq.q: How loud are they on high?
faq.a: The quoted low-speed levels of about 23 to 24 dB do not apply on high, where any of them becomes clearly audible. Use auto mode so the fan only ramps up when the sensor needs it.

They are a real recurring cost, and larger models cost more per swap. Check the genuine filter price before choosing a model, and avoid unknown third-party filters that may not match the electrostatic design.

faq.q: Do I need the DustMagnet for pets?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It helps with floor-level dust and keeps it from resettling, but the 311i Max with its washable pre-filter handles pet dander well in most homes.
